title: "quarto-index sort-key misuse probe"
from: markdown-smart
filters:

# Three ways to misuse a sort key

Each mark below draws exactly one report, and each report is about the mark
rather than about any one back-end — so every one of them reaches an author
writing to a format that builds no index at all.

A sort key on a mark that indexes nothing has nothing to sort. The mark is
empty and carries no `entry=`, so there is no entry for the key to place:
[]{.index sort="Nowhere"}

A sort key deeper than the entry it sorts. The entry is the visible term,
which is always a single level, so the second sort level places nothing:
[Solo]{.index sort="first!second"}.

One printed index level given two different sort keys files in two places,
which is not something an index can do. The two marks below do not write the
same entry — each carries its own sub-entry — but they share their first
level, and it is that level each of them writes a key for. Sharing a level is
enough: both back-ends order an index level by level, so the shared level
would file under one key here and another there, and the term would print
twice. The first mark in document order wins and the second is reported:
[Ambivalence]{.index entry="Ambivalence!first" sort="Aaa"} and later
[Ambivalence]{.index entry="Ambivalence!second" sort="Bbb"}. A third mark
repeating the rival key adds nothing for the author to fix, so it draws no
second report: [Ambivalence]{.index entry="Ambivalence!third" sort="Bbb"}.

# A sort key for a level the back-end cannot store

The LaTeX back-end stores three levels and folds everything past the third
into it. A sort key written for one of the folded levels goes where that level
went — there is nothing left for it to place — and the fold warning already
names the entry. What must not happen is the opposite: an entry whose third
level was never given a key of its own must not come out carrying one, which
is what comparing the key against the folded text rather than against the
level it was written for produces.

No key for the third level, so the folded level carries none:
[Deep]{.index entry="one!two!three!four" sort="Alpha"}.

A key written for the third level, which the fold keeps:
[Deeper]{.index entry="aa!bb!cc!dd" sort="aa!bb!Ckey"}.
